words.def: A bee is a small striped insect that buzzes around flowers and makes honey.
words.sentence: A bee buzzed around the flowers in the garden.
words.adultDef: A bee is a small insect with yellow and black stripes and wings. Bees fly from flower to flower to collect nectar, and they make honey. A bee can sting, so we watch them but never touch!

words.def: A tree is a tall plant with a thick trunk, branches and leaves.
ask: What kinds of trees do you know?
words.sentence: The koala was asleep up in the gum tree.
words.adultDef: A tree is a very tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves. In Australia we have lots of gum trees – koalas live in them and eat their leaves. Trees give us shade on a hot day.

words.def: A seed is a tiny part of a plant. If you put it in soil and water it, a new plant can grow.
ask: What happens when you plant a seed and water it?
words.sentence: I planted a sunflower seed in a pot.
words.adultDef: A seed is the tiny part of a plant that a new plant grows from. You plant a seed in the soil, give it water and sun, and it grows! Watermelons and apples have seeds inside.

words.def: Green is a colour, like grass and leaves.
ask: What things can you think of that are green?
words.sentence: The grass is green after the rain.
words.adultDef: Green is a colour. Grass, leaves, frogs and broccoli are green. If you mix blue paint and yellow paint together, you get green!

words.def: Feet are at the bottom of your legs. You walk on them. One is a foot, two are feet.
ask: What do you wear on your feet?
words.sentence: I wiggled my feet in the sand at the beach.
words.adultDef: Your feet are at the end of your legs. You stand, walk and run on them. You have one foot on each leg – when we talk about two of them, we say feet .

words.def: A sheep is a farm animal with thick, woolly fur. It says baa!
words.sentence: The farmer has lots of sheep on his farm.
words.adultDef: A sheep is a farm animal with a thick, woolly coat. Sheep say 'baa!' Farmers cut off the wool and we use it to make warm jumpers. Australia has lots and lots of sheep!
